article.headline: Cloudflare Grows Sales 35.9% As It Pushes Into Post-Quantum Security
article.deck: The cloud-security leader trades 2.9% above the 332.32 buy point of a five-week cup, inside the buy range up to 348.94.
body: Cloudflare sells cloud services that protect and speed up the businesses that use it. Its security lineup covers web application firewalls, bot management, defense against distributed denial-of-service attacks, API security and encryption, and it also sells tools that make applications run faster. Customers use it to guard public and private clouds, their own data centers, software-as-a-service apps and connected devices.

Sales are the growth story. Revenue rose 35.9% to $696.1 million in the June quarter. The three quarters before that came in at $562.0 million, $614.5 million and $639.8 million, each larger than the one before. The June quarter is the only one of the four with a year-over-year comparison, and it shows revenue growth of better than a third.

Profits are another matter. Cloudflare lost 48 cents a share in the June quarter, after losses of 7 cents and 3 cents in the two prior periods and breakeven in the September 2025 quarter. The next report is due Oct. 29.

The market pays up anyway. Cloudflare carries a $121.7 billion market value and trades at 203.97 times forward earnings. Shares are up 73.4% this year and 57.3% over 12 months. The stock ranks 90 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 5.5% below its high.

Cloudflare broke out Sept. 17 past the 332.32 buy point of a five-week cup that was 18.9% deep, with its high on Aug. 13 and a low of 269.30 on Sept. 2. Volume on the breakout was just 0.88 times average, a soft start. Fifteen sessions later, the stock closed Thursday at 341.89, down 1.08, or 0.3%, in volume 0.70 times average. That is 2.9% above the buy point and inside the range that tops out at 348.94.

The stock is 7.7% below its 52-week high of 370.35. It trades 8.7% above its 50-day line at 314.47 and above the 21-day line at 338.95, and it has climbed 27.4% in three months. The 200-day line sits far below at 238.31, and the stock trades 43.5% above it. Thursday's dip came in light volume, and the close left the stock 2.9% above the buy point with the 21-day line just below.

Recent headlines track the business. One Thursday weighed the stock's valuation after a post-quantum security push, another looked at a new trust and data push, and a third explained why the shares rallied nearly 14% in September.
article.watch: The Oct. 29 earnings report, and whether the stock holds its 21-day line at 338.95.

article.headline: SpaceX Rises 2% After Hours As Spectrum Acquisition News Slams Telecoms
article.deck: After-hours trade keeps the IPO-base breakout inside the buy range from the 158.23 buy point to 166.14, after a 4.2% drop in the regular session.
body: SpaceX traded at 163.74 at 5:25 p.m. ET, up 3.17, or 2.0%, in after-hours action. That followed a regular session in which the stock fell 7.03, or 4.2%, to 160.57. Volume came to 68.5 million shares, 0.68 times the 50-day average, so the selling came on light trade. The close sits 1.5% above the 158.23 buy point of a two-week IPO base that was 8.1% deep, and the after-hours price is still inside the buy range, which tops out at 166.14. The stock cleared the buy point Oct. 2 in volume 1.24 times average.

SpaceX has traded 82 sessions. The IPO base formed after a bigger correction, and the stock remains 28.8% below its June 16 high of 225.64, which came before a slide to 104.83 by Aug. 3. Four sessions past the breakout, the stock is 12.1% above its 50-day line at 143.23 and above the 21-day line at 154.66. It ranks 67 of 99 on the desk's list for relative strength, and the RS line is 26.5% off its high. Shares are up 8.8% in a month.

The company is still losing money. It lost 9 cents a share on revenue of $7.81 billion in the June quarter, after a 41-cent loss on $4.69 billion in the March quarter. The market values SpaceX at $2.12 trillion, or 83.39 times forward earnings. The next report is due Nov. 3.

Late Thursday headlines said telecom stocks tumbled on SpaceX spectrum acquisition news, with one saying the SpaceX move slammed Verizon and AT&T. Another said OpenAI took another executive from SpaceX as it pushes into global sales.
A close back under 158.23 would turn this into a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Whether the after-hours gain holds into Friday and keeps the stock inside the 158.23-166.14 buy range.

article.headline: AbbVie Nears High After Cancer Drug Wins Two FDA Breakthrough Tags
article.deck: The flat-base breakout past a 267.57 buy point is one day old and inside the buy range up to 280.95.
body: AbbVie rose 1.06, or 0.4%, to 272.42 Thursday, a day after clearing the 267.57 buy point of a 10-week flat base. Volume ran 0.92 times the 50-day average. The base was 9.8% deep, with its high on July 29 and its low on Aug. 6. Wednesday's breakout came in volume 1.29 times average, and the stock now sits 1.8% above the buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 280.95.

Shares are 0.9% below the 52-week high of 274.94. The stock trades 5.4% above its 50-day line at 258.51, and the 21-day line sits at 264.10. The RS line is 2.5% below its high, and the stock ranks 62 of 99 on the desk's list. AbbVie is up 19.2% this year and 17.0% over 12 months.

June-quarter earnings rose 290.4% to 2.03 a share as revenue grew 10.2% to $16.99 billion. The three quarters before that came in at 10 cents, 1.02 and 39 cents a share. The stock trades at 16.76 times forward earnings, for a $481.4 billion market value. AbbVie reports again Oct. 30.

Headlines Wednesday and Thursday said the FDA gave AbbVie's telisotuzumab adizutecan, or Temab-A, two Breakthrough Therapy designations, for colorectal cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. Another headline said the drugmaker cut the risk of progression or death in frontline DLBCL by 51%. A separate piece asked how long AbbVie can keep paying out more than it earns.
A move above 274.94 would put the stock at a new high; a close under 267.57 would stall the breakout.

article.headline: Micron Drops 4.8% As Samsung's Record Profit Fails To Lift It
article.deck: The flat-base breakout has stalled at the 1036.23 buy point, with the stock closing 39 cents under it.
body: Micron fell 52.16, or 4.8%, to 1035.84 Thursday in volume 0.99 times its 50-day average. That left the memory chipmaker 39 cents below the 1036.23 buy point of a five-week flat base that was 14.3% deep. The buy range runs to 1088.04. Micron cleared the buy point Sept. 21, but volume that day was just 0.82 times average, and 13 sessions later the stock has given back the whole move.

The flat base formed after a bigger correction: Micron remains 17.5% below its June 25 high of 1255.00, which preceded a drop to 737.88 by July 29. The stock closed just under its 21-day line at 1038.62 and 6.4% above its 50-day line at 973.10. It ranks 97 of 99 on the desk's list, though the RS line is 19.1% off its high. Shares are up 262.9% this year and 457.8% over 12 months.

Earnings in the May quarter jumped 1,368.5% to 24.67 a share, and revenue rose 345.7% to $41.46 billion. Quarterly EPS over the four periods shown ran 2.83, 4.60, 12.07 and 24.67. The stock trades at 5.02 times forward earnings, with a $1.17 trillion market value. The next report is due Dec. 23.

Headlines Thursday said Samsung's operating profit hit a record $80 billion but did not give Micron a lift, with one adding that Samsung's growth, like Micron's memory prices, is slowing. Another reported that Micron workers in Taiwan authorized strike action over a bonus-scheme dispute.
A close back above 1036.23 restores the breakout; a slide toward the 50-day line at 973.10 would mean it has failed.

June-quarter earnings rose 9.3% to 4.68 a share, and revenue grew 10.5% to $11.99 billion. EPS in the three prior quarters came in at 4.27, 5.21 and 4.43. The stock trades at 23.64 times forward earnings for a $241.1 billion market value. Thermo Fisher reports Oct. 21.
